name: Venice.ai
tagline: Private AI chat, image generation and code help running open-source models with no server-side logging.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product here is two things stacked: a clean chat interface with browser-local history, and hosted GPUs running open-weight models that will answer questions a corporate assistant refuses. An agent can rebuild the first half in a session, streaming from a local Ollama into a chat UI that stores threads in IndexedDB and never touches a server you don't own. The second half is where it breaks down: the useful large open models want more VRAM than a laptop has, and image generation locally means installing a whole separate stack and waiting. Point your build at a hosted inference API instead and you have quietly reintroduced the exact third party whose logs you were trying to avoid. So: real DIY win if you own a GPU or are content with small models, otherwise you are paying for someone else's hardware and their promise not to keep records.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first chat app that streams from your own Ollama models and keeps every thread in the browser, with no account and no server-side storage.
requirements: Ollama installed locally with at least one pulled model
A machine with a decent GPU or Apple Silicon if you want usable speed
Optional: a local ComfyUI or Stable Diffusion install for image generation
whatYouLose: Access to large open models like the 70B+ and reasoning-tier ones you cannot run at home
Image generation that works instantly without you babysitting a diffusion install
Web search grounding, document upload handling and API keys for other tools
Mobile access, since your build lives on one machine unless you expose it yourself
Someone else's uptime, model updates and stated no-logs policy instead of your own discipline
moatNotes: The privacy claim is a trust asset, not a technical one. You cannot verify it, which is exactly why running the model yourself is the only real version of the promise.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because GPUs are expensive and inconvenient. Paying a monthly fee to get uncensored open models at speed, from any device, with a credible privacy posture and no setup, beats a self-hosted rig for most people who just want to ask things without being lectured or logged. The subscription is renting hardware and a policy, and both are hard to reproduce on a laptop.
notes: The interface is a weekend; the GPUs are not. If your hardware can run the model you want, self-hosting is strictly better on privacy grounds because you stop having to trust anybody.
prompt:
Build a local-first private AI chat app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all chat storage, in the browser only
- Ollama as the model backend, reached at OLLAMA_URL from .env.local, default http://localhost:11434
- No database, no auth library, no analytics, no external API calls of any kind

Features in scope:
1. Sidebar of conversations: create, rename, delete, all stored in IndexedDB. Nothing leaves the machine.
2. Chat view with streaming token output. Proxy Ollama's /api/chat through a Next.js route handler and stream the response to the client with ReadableStream.
3. Model picker populated live from Ollama's /api/tags. Remember the last used model per conversation.
4. Per conversation system prompt, editable in a collapsible panel, plus temperature and context length sliders. Persist them with the conversation.
5. Markdown rendering with fenced code blocks, syntax highlighting, and a copy button per block.
6. Stop generation button that aborts the fetch mid stream and keeps the partial reply.
7. Regenerate last reply, and edit any user message to fork the thread from that point.
8. Export a conversation to Markdown and JSON, and import JSON back.
9. Global search across all stored messages, client side.
10. Dark mode by default, keyboard shortcuts: Enter to send, Shift+Enter newline, Cmd+K for search.

Explicitly out of scope: image generation, web search, file uploads, RAG, hosted model providers, user accounts, any server-side persistence.

Deliverables: working app on npm run dev, a .env.local.example with OLLAMA_URL, and a README that states plainly which data lives where and that clearing browser storage deletes everything.
